when: Digital footnotes and all endnotes require ‘Notes’.
Print-only footnotes must have no heading.
rules.why: G-2: medium and note type change the expected heading, not the check.

rules.quote: Footnotes are preferable for digital content, which has no set page length.
rules.violation_condition: Digital content uses endnotes rather than the preferred footnotes.
when: The content is digital.
rules.why: The page expressly identifies a preferred alternative.

covers.quote: In print, footnotes work well if you only have a few citations.

rules.quote: Endnotes work better for print, which has a set page length, because they don’t take up space on a page.
rules.specification: Treat this as a preference, not a prohibition on print footnotes. The page expressly accepts footnotes for a few citations.
rules.violation_condition: Print content uses footnotes where the page's preference is for endnotes.
when: The content is printed.
Footnotes are an accepted option when there are only a few citations.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: preserve the stated print preference with its accepted footnote case.

rules.quote: In print, if you have sections written by different authors or on different subjects, include a list of endnotes at the end of each section.
rules.violation_condition: A print work with sections by different authors or on different subjects collects its endnotes elsewhere instead of at the end of each section.
when: The work is printed and uses endnotes.
Its sections have different authors or subjects.
rules.why: G-2: retain the conditions on section-level endnote placement.

covers.quote: Use reference numbers instead of symbols in most content.
Reference symbols are best for content with many numbers, such as content with mathematical equations.
Use symbols if there’s a risk that users will confuse superscript numbers for exponents.

rules.quote: Use numbers for reference markers in most content
rules.violation_condition: Reference markers use symbols rather than numbers without the stated reason for preferring symbols.
when: Numbers are the default.
Symbols are preferred for number-heavy content, especially where superscript reference numbers could be confused with exponents.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: marker choice is one preference with a number-heavy exception.

rules.quote: In content that uses a lot of citations, restart numbering on each page of digital content or in each section of a document.
rules.specification: The page does not define how many citations count as ‘a lot’.
rules.violation_condition: Citation-heavy content continues reference numbering across digital pages or document sections instead of restarting it.
when: The content uses a lot of citations.
Restart on each digital page or in each document section.
rules.why: G-2: retain both medium-dependent restart boundaries in one numbering check.

rules.violation_condition: Symbol reference markers point to endnotes rather than footnotes.
when: Reference markers are symbols.

when: Reference markers are symbols.
rules.why: G-2: doubling extends the same symbol-sequence check.

rules.quote: Restart the symbols on each page.
rules.violation_condition: A page continues the previous page's reference-symbol sequence rather than starting again.
when: Reference markers are symbols.
rules.why: The restart boundary is distinct from the order of symbols within a page.

rules.quote: In digital content, hyperlink the reference marker to help users access the note.

when: The marker identifies a footnote or endnote.

rules.violation_condition: The reference marker and the beginning of a footnote or endnote are separated by no space or by more than one space.
when: A reference marker precedes a footnote or endnote.
rules.why: Spacing is independently flaggable from marker position.

rules.quote: Don’t use more than one reference marker in the same place, such as when citing 2 works.

when: A footnote or endnote cites more than one work.
rules.why: The note's entry separator is independently flaggable from multiple in-text markers.

when: The same work is cited more than once.
rules.why: A new marker for each occurrence is distinct from shortening the repeated reference.

covers.quote: Short forms include only the author’s family name (or authoring organisation name) and the title of the source.

rules.quote: In the notes, use a shortened form of the citation after the first mention, instead of citing the full source again.
rules.violation_condition: A repeated citation repeats the full source details or includes fields beyond the author family name or organisation name and title.
when: The work has already been cited in full.
If endnotes are collected by section, give the full citation at the first occurrence in each section.
Apply the stated rules for multiple authors, organisations, translated works, interviews and social media.

rules.quote: Use the shortened form when appropriate.

rules.quote: Don’t use the Latin abbreviations ‘ibid.’, ‘op cit.’ or ‘loc cit.’ for repeated citations.

rules.why: The named prohibited forms make a distinct lexical check.

rules.quote: Write the initials of given names before writing the family name of the authors, editors or translators.

rules.violation_condition: Full stops occur between an author's, editor's or translator's initials.
when: Personal-name initials appear in a citation.
rules.why: Initial punctuation is distinct from name order.

rules.quote: When you have more than 2 authors, use the Latin term ‘et al.’ (meaning ‘and others’) in short citations.
rules.violation_condition: A short citation with more than 2 authors does not use the first author's family name followed by ‘et al.’, or a short citation with up to 2 authors incorrectly replaces a name with ‘et al.’.
when: The citation is shortened.
rules.why: G-2: author count determines the form of one short-author-list check.

rules.quote: Don’t use italics for ‘et al.’.
rules.violation_condition: ‘et al.’ is italicised in a citation.
when: ‘et al.’ appears in a citation.
rules.why: Typography is distinct from deciding when to abbreviate an author list.

covers.quote: If you have used the shortened form of an organisation’s name in your content, use it in your references. Use the shortened form followed by the spelt-out version in parentheses.

rules.quote: The first note to cite the organisation as author gives the name in full, and introduces the shortened form.
rules.violation_condition: The first note for an organisation author fails to pair its full name with its shortened form, or puts them in the wrong order for the stated prior-use case.
when: An organisation has a shortened form used in the references.
Normally introduce the full name followed by the shortened form.
If the shortened form has already been used in the content, put it first and the spelt-out name in parentheses.
rules.why: G-2: prior use changes the order of the same first-reference name pair.

covers.quote: Use the shortened form in subsequent references.
If the organisation name has an abbreviation, use that in the short citation.

rules.quote: If the author is an organisation, short citations use the shortened form of the organisation’s name.
rules.violation_condition: A subsequent organisation-author citation spells out the name instead of using its available shortened form.
when: The organisation has a suitable shortened form.
For agency names, the agency must use the shortened form regularly.
rules.why: G-4: consolidate the general rule and its later restatements.

rules.quote: Use the name that appears on the source.
rules.violation_condition: A citation replaces the organisation name on the source with a later or otherwise different organisation name.
when: An organisation is the author, including an agency that has changed names.
rules.why: This is a source-name accuracy check, not a rule to modernise agency names.

rules.quote: Only use a shortened form of an agency’s name if the agency uses it regularly.
rules.specification: Determining regular agency use requires an external authority or maintained list.
rules.violation_condition: A citation uses an agency-name abbreviation that the agency does not regularly use.
when: An agency name is shortened.
rules.why: Eligibility of an abbreviation is distinct from its introduction and subsequent use.

covers.quote: Do this even if you have not introduced the shortened form before.

rules.quote: To avoid repetition of long names, use the shortened form for the name of the website after the title.
rules.specification: The page does not define ‘long’; applicability should be reviewed rather than assigned an invented length threshold.
rules.violation_condition: A citation repeats a long organisation name as the website name after already giving it as the author, instead of using the shortened website name.
when: The same organisation supplies the author name and website name.
The shortened website name can be used even if not previously introduced.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: retain the special repetition case and its introduction exception.

covers.quote: Use lower case for all other words.

rules.quote: Capitalise all proper nouns, the names of periodicals and the first word of the title or type of work.
rules.violation_condition: A cited title or work type fails to capitalise a proper noun or first word, fails to capitalise a periodical name, or capitalises other words that should be lower case.
when: Apply the separate instruction to retain an organisation's capitalisation of a website name.
rules.why: G-2: upper- and lower-case cases are one citation-capitalisation check.

rules.quote: Use commas to separate elements.
rules.violation_condition: Citation elements lack their separating commas or use a different separator where the reference format calls for commas.
when: Apply special internal formats such as volume(issue):pages, parenthetical roles and semicolons between separate works.
rules.why: Keep element punctuation separate from element order.

rules.quote: Use a full stop at the end of the reference.
rules.violation_condition: A reference lacks its final full stop.
when: For print-only online-source references, the URL follows this final full stop.
The full stop is also added to National Archives of Australia citations.
rules.why: Final punctuation is an independent citation-format check.

covers.quote: Don’t use italics if the reference is:
a book chapter
an article
a poem
an episode
a page that is part of a series or a similar division.
use italics for the name of the series, book or periodical.
If the title is in italics or quotation marks in the full citation, use italics or quotation marks in the short citation.

rules.quote: Use italics for the formal title of a complete published work.
rules.violation_condition: A complete published work's formal title is not italicised, or a component title such as an article or chapter is italicised instead of remaining non-italic.
when: Italicise a containing series, book or periodical name.
Do not italicise a chapter, article, poem, episode, or page forming part of a series or similar division.
Retain the same italics treatment in a shortened citation.
rules.why: G-2: work type and full versus short citation are conditions on title typography.

rules.quote: If it’s part of a publication, use single quotation marks around the title
rules.violation_condition: The title of a component of a publication lacks enclosing single quotation marks or uses double quotation marks instead.
when: The cited item is part of a publication.
Retain the quotation marks in short citations.
rules.why: Quotation marks are independently checkable from italics on the containing work.

covers.quote: This includes retaining misspellings and using any American spelling variations.

rules.quote: Use the original spelling for all titles and periodical names.
rules.violation_condition: A cited title or periodical name changes the source's spelling, including correcting a misspelling or replacing an American spelling.
when: Preserve misspellings and American spelling variations.
rules.why: G-4: retain the spelling-preservation explanation within one rule.

covers.quote: Short citations don’t include any subtitles.

rules.quote: Use the shortened form of a title when you refer to the same work more than once.
rules.specification: Subtitle omission is explicit, but the page does not specify how far a main title should otherwise be shortened.
rules.violation_condition: A subsequent citation repeats a title that should be shortened, including retaining its subtitle.
when: The same work is cited again in a short citation.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: subtitle omission specifies the same shortened-title requirement.

rules.quote: For works without a date, write ‘n.d.’ instead of the date of publication.
rules.violation_condition: A citation to an undated work leaves the publication-date position blank or uses a form other than ‘n.d.’.
when: The work has no publication date.
rules.why: A missing source date triggers one prescribed replacement.

rules.quote: For works like newspaper articles and social media posts, include the full date – not just the year – in the reference.
rules.specification: Newspaper articles and social media posts are explicit cases; the page's templates identify further full-date source types.
rules.violation_condition: A reference to a date-specific work gives only the year or omits part of the full publication date.
when: The source is a newspaper article, social media post or another source type for which this page specifies Day Month Year.
rules.why: G-2: source type determines whether a full publication date is required.

covers.quote: Do this when you use the full title of the source (the first time you include it in a note).
Don’t hyperlink titles in short citations.
Hyperlink the name of the website.
Hyperlink the title of the webpage.
If you read the book online, hyperlink the title.

rules.quote: Unless the source is behind a paywall, hyperlink the title of works available online.
rules.violation_condition: A full citation to an online source not behind a paywall lacks a title hyperlink, or a short citation contains a title hyperlink.
when: Hyperlink the full title at its first full citation.
The requirement does not apply to sources behind a paywall or print-only documents.
Do not hyperlink titles in short citations.
For an entire website, hyperlink the website name.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: full versus short citations and online-source variants determine the same title-link check.

covers.quote: You don’t need to include the URL in references in digital content.

rules.quote: If the document is print only, include a URL after the reference. Put the URL after the final full stop.
rules.violation_condition: A print-only reference to an online work omits its URL or places the URL before the reference's final full stop.
when: The citing document is print only.
The cited source is online.
Digital references need not display a URL.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: printed URL presentation has a digital-content exception.

covers.quote: When citing a website, include the date you accessed it.
Always include the date you accessed the site at the end of the reference.
Always include the date you accessed the site at the end of the reference.
Include the date you accessed it at the end of the reference.
Include the date you accessed the article or post at the end of the reference.
As books are published in editions, you don’t need to include an accessed date.

rules.quote: Include the date you accessed the work.
rules.violation_condition: An online-source reference omits the access date or fails to place it at the end where specified.
when: The source was accessed online.
Books do not require an access date because they are published in editions.
rules.why: G-2, G-3 and G-4: consolidate access-date restatements and the book exception.

covers.quote: Don’t link to PDFs or other downloadable documents. Instead link to the page that hosts the document.
If you’re citing a PDF or spreadsheet, avoid linking directly to the document. Instead link to the webpage that hosts the document.
If you’re citing a PDF, avoid linking directly to the PDF. Instead link to the page that hosts the PDF.
If you’re citing a PDF, avoid linking directly to the PDF. Instead link to the page that hosts the PDF.
If you’re citing a PDF, avoid linking directly to the PDF. Instead link to the page that hosts the PDF.
If you’re citing a PDF, avoid linking directly to the PDF. Instead link to the page that hosts the PDF.

rules.quote: If you’re citing a PDF, avoid linking directly to the PDF. Instead link to the landing page where the PDF is hosted.
rules.violation_condition: A citation links directly to a PDF or other downloadable document when a hosting landing page is available.
when: A hosting or landing page exists.
If a PDF has no landing page, link directly to the PDF.
The page repeats the hosting-page preference for spreadsheets and other downloadable documents.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: consolidate the repeated link-target preference and no-landing-page exception.

covers.quote: Follow ‘PDF’ with the file size in kilobytes (KB) or megabytes (MB).
Include both of these additional details in the linked text.

rules.quote: If the PDF doesn’t have a landing page, link to the PDF and include ‘PDF’ in square brackets after the title.
rules.violation_condition: A direct PDF citation without a landing page lacks the bracketed PDF label and KB or MB file size after the title, or leaves those details outside the linked text.
when: The PDF has no landing page and is linked directly.
rules.why: G-2: label, size and link extent define one direct-PDF link presentation.

covers.quote: For journal articles, include the DOI if possible.
Include a DOI if the book has one.

rules.quote: If the document has a DOI, include it in the citation. Put it at the end of the citation and include the shortened form ‘doi’ in lower case before it.
rules.violation_condition: A source with a DOI lacks it in the citation, places it somewhere other than the end, or uses a prefix other than lower-case ‘doi’.
when: The cited document has a DOI.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: consolidate DOI inclusion and presentation across source types.

covers.quote: the letter ‘p’ and the page number to cite one page
the letters ‘pp’ and the page number range to cite a range of pages.

rules.quote: To cite a specific page or page range in a work, add:
rules.violation_condition: A specific-page locator lacks ‘p’ before one page number or ‘pp’ before a page range, or uses the wrong one.
when: The locator identifies a specific page or page range, rather than the journal article's publication page span.
rules.why: G-2: single-page and page-range cases determine one locator-prefix check.

rules.quote: If the citation has a volume number, an issue number and page numbers follow the format: volume(issue):page–page.
rules.violation_condition: A citation containing volume, issue and page numbers does not present them as volume(issue):page–page.
when: The citation contains a volume number, issue number and page numbers.
rules.why: This is a specific internal numerical-format check.

rules.quote: To cite a specific page of this work, add the page number at the end.
rules.violation_condition: A citation to a specific page of an article with a publication page range omits the additional pinpoint page or places it before the end.
when: A particular page within the cited article is being referenced.
rules.why: Pinpoint placement is distinct from formatting the article's publication page range.

covers.quote: Rule: Organisation Name Title of media release: subtitle of media release [media release], Organisation Name, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.

rules.quote: Rule: A Author and B Author, Title of media release: subtitle of media release [media release], Organisation Name, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.
rules.violation_condition: A media-release reference omits its ‘[media release]’ designation or issuing organisation, or assigns the author role incorrectly when no personal author is listed.
when: Use listed personal authors when present.
With no listed authors, use the organisation as author.
Apply the general date, access-date, hyperlink and punctuation rules separately.
rules.why: G-2: author availability changes the same media-release citation structure.

rules.quote: Follow the authoring details on the title page of the document.
rules.violation_condition: A report citation's authoring details disagree with the report's title page.
when: The source has a title page.
rules.why: The instruction defines the authoritative source for a text property.

covers.quote: Rule: A Author or Agency Name (Abbreviation), Title of report: subtitle of report, Agency Name or Abbreviation, Name of Government, unpublished, accessed Day Month Year.

rules.quote: Rule: A Author or Agency Name (Abbreviation), Title of report: subtitle of report, Agency Name or Abbreviation, Name of Government, Year, accessed Day Month Year.
rules.violation_condition: A reference to a government-agency report omits the agency or name of government, or fails to identify an unpublished agency report as ‘unpublished’ in the date position.
when: The report is by a government agency.
Use the unpublished variant when the report is unpublished.
Access dates apply to sources accessed online.
rules.why: G-2: publication status changes the same government-report format.

rules.quote: Rule: A Author or Agency Name (Abbreviation), ‘Title of report: subtitle of report’, Name of Series, catalogue number, Agency Name or Abbreviation, Name of Government, Year, accessed Day Month Year.
rules.violation_condition: A report-in-series reference omits the series name or catalogue number, or places those series details outside their position between report title and agency.
when: The government report is part of a series.
rules.why: Keep the additional series-identification check distinct from general government-report details.

rules.quote: Rule: A Author or Organisation Name (Abbreviation), Title of report: subtitle of report, report to Agency Name, Organisation Name or Abbreviation, Year.
rules.violation_condition: A report prepared for a government agency fails to identify the recipient with ‘report to’ after the title or omits the producing organisation.
when: The report was prepared for a government agency by an external author or organisation.
rules.why: The recipient relationship is an additional source-specific element.

covers.quote: use the name of the parliament as the author
include the paper number.

rules.quote: Rule: Name of Parliament, Title of document: subtitle of document, Parl Paper X, Name of Government, Year.
rules.violation_condition: A document cited from a bound parliamentary volume does not use the parliament as author or omits its ‘Parl Paper’ number or government identification.
when: The document was accessed as part of a bound volume from a parliamentary sitting.
Individually accessed documents use their ordinary document-type citation instead.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: consolidate the bound-volume instructions and their template.

covers.quote: To cite a record of what was said in parliament verbatim, as recorded in Hansard, use the volume and page number. Volume numbers are before the colon; page numbers are after.

rules.quote: Rule: Name of Parliamentary Committee or House, Debates, Year, volume:page–page.
rules.violation_condition: A Hansard reference omits the committee or house, ‘Debates’, volume or page locator, or fails to put volume before and pages after a colon.
when: The source is a verbatim parliamentary record in Hansard.
rules.why: G-4: the prose and template specify one Hansard locator structure.

covers.quote: To cite the official records of proceedings in each house of parliament, include the volume or issue number and the page number. Issue numbers are in parentheses. Volume numbers are outside of parentheses.

rules.quote: Rule: Name of Parliamentary House, Journalor Votes and Proceedings, Year, (issue) or volume:page–page.
rules.violation_condition: An official parliamentary-proceedings reference omits its house, record title, volume or issue, or pages, or puts a volume in parentheses or leaves an issue outside parentheses.
when: The source is an official record of proceedings in a parliamentary house.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: issue and volume are alternative cases of the same proceedings locator.

rules.quote: Rule: A Author, Title of data set [data set], Name of Website website, Year, accessed Day Month Year.
rules.violation_condition: A data-set reference lacks the ‘[data set]’ designation after its title.
when: The source is a data set; apply source-specific ABS instructions where relevant.
rules.why: The designation is the additional requirement not already covered by common reference structure.

rules.quote: Follow the ABS advice for information to include, but adjust capitalisation and punctuation to be in line with the rest of the notes in your content.
rules.specification: The required source-specific information must be obtained from the ABS guide; this page supplies only the adaptation principle.
rules.violation_condition: A reference to ABS material omits information required by ABS referencing advice or retains ABS capitalisation and punctuation that conflict with the surrounding documentary–note style.
when: The cited material is from the Australian Bureau of Statistics.
rules.why: G-2: ABS information requirements apply with an explicit local-style adjustment.

rules.quote: Follow this advice exactly, but add a full stop at the end of the citation.
rules.specification: The external NAA guide supplies the exact format. Final full-stop absence is handled by the general final-punctuation rule.
rules.violation_condition: A reference to an NAA-held record departs from the National Archives of Australia's prescribed referencing format.
when: The source is a record held by the National Archives of Australia.
rules.why: G-2: preserve the externally specified citation format and the stated punctuation adjustment.

covers.quote: However, if you refer to content only found on a particular webpage on the website, you need to pinpoint the relevant webpage or webpage content in the citation.

rules.quote: Only cite an entire website if you cannot pinpoint the material to a specific webpage or webpage content.
rules.violation_condition: A citation identifies only an entire website although the referenced material can be pinpointed to a particular webpage or content item.
when: An entire-website citation is acceptable for a general resource that cannot be pinpointed.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: both sentences govern the same citation-specificity decision.

covers.quote: Use the same capitalisation as the organisation uses for the name of a website.

rules.quote: Use the same capitalisation as the organisation uses for the name of a website.
rules.violation_condition: A cited website name uses different capitalisation from the organisation's own form.
when: A website name appears in a reference.
rules.why: G-4: consolidate the identical website-name capitalisation instructions.

covers.quote: If you include the homepage URL, do not include the word ‘website’ in square brackets.
Include the word ‘website’ after the name of the website, unless the name of the website is a URL – for example ‘WA.gov.au’.
When citing a document hosted on a webpage, but not the webpage itself, don’t include the word ‘website’ in the citation.

rules.quote: Include the word ‘website’ after the name of the website in square brackets, unless you include the URL for the homepage.
rules.violation_condition: An online reference omits or misformats the required website designation, retains ‘[website]’ beside an entire-site homepage URL, or adds ‘website’ when citing an online document rather than the webpage.
when: An entire-site reference uses ‘[website]’ after the website name unless a homepage URL is included.
A webpage reference uses ‘website’ without square brackets after the website name, unless that name is itself a URL.
A reference to a document hosted on a webpage does not include ‘website’.
rules.why: G-2: cited-object type and URL presentation determine one website-designation check.

rules.quote: For videos published online, hyperlink the title of the video and file format.
rules.violation_condition: An online-video reference's hyperlink excludes the file-format designation.
when: The reference is to a video published online.
rules.why: The link's extension over the format label is additional to the general title-link requirement.

rules.quote: Rule: C Creator or Owner of Video, ‘Title of video’ [video], Name of Channel or Owning Organisation, Name of Website website, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.
rules.violation_condition: An online-video citation omits its creator or owner, ‘[video]’ designation, or channel or owning organisation, or puts those identifying elements in the wrong roles.
when: The cited source is an online video.
rules.why: Retain the source-specific creator, medium and channel structure without duplicating common date and link checks.

covers.quote: Don’t include this information or a reference marker in the caption or title to the table or figure.

rules.quote: For tables and images (such as graphs) you’re using in the content, attribute the source in the notes below the table or image (also called a ‘figure’).
rules.violation_condition: A reproduced table or image has no source attribution in notes below it, or places that attribution in its caption or title instead.
when: The table or image is used in the content.
Photographs, illustrations and other works of art have the separate extended-caption treatment.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: required and prohibited attribution locations form one placement check.

rules.quote: Don’t include this information or a reference marker in the caption or title to the table or figure.
rules.violation_condition: A table or figure caption or title contains a reference marker.
when: The table or figure is reproduced in the content.
rules.why: A prohibited marker can occur independently of correctly placed source-attribution notes.

rules.quote: Rule: Source: Adapted from Source.
rules.specification: Apply ‘Adapted from’ to adapted material, not indiscriminately to unchanged reproductions.
rules.violation_condition: A source note for an adapted table or figure does not identify the source with ‘Source: Adapted from’.
when: The table or figure has been adapted from another source.
rules.why: The template prescribes the source-note lead-in; its adaptation wording limits applicability.

covers.quote: Attribute works of art (such as photographs) using an extended caption that includes:
the full details of the work of art
copyright and permission information if necessary.

rules.quote: Rule: Creator Full Name, Title or description of work [medium], Name of Website website, Exhibition or Gallery, Location of Gallery, Year, © Creator, courtesy: Creator or Gallery, accessed Date Month Year.
rules.violation_condition: A reproduced work of art lacks an extended caption giving its creator's full name, title or description, medium and applicable identifying, copyright or permission details.
when: The work of art, such as a photograph or illustration, is used in the content.
Include gallery, location, website, copyright and permission details as applicable.
If merely discussing the work without reproducing it, use an ordinary reference marker and note.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: consolidate the artwork-caption instruction, its required details and template.

covers.quote: If a post or article doesn’t list an author, use the name of the blog, newspaper or magazine.
Rule: Name of Blog, Newspaper or Magazine, ‘Title of article: subtitle of article’, Name of Newspaper or Magazine, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.

rules.quote: Rule: A Author, ‘Title of article: subtitle of article’, Name of Blog, Newspaper or Magazine, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.
rules.violation_condition: A blog-post, newspaper or magazine reference omits its publication name or fails to use the publication as author when no author is listed.
when: Use a listed author where one exists.
If no author is listed, use the blog, newspaper or magazine name as author.
rules.why: G-2: listed-author and no-author cases belong to one publication-attribution check.

rules.quote: Rule: A Author, ‘Re: Title of post: subtitle of post’ [blog comment], Name of Blog, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.
rules.violation_condition: A blog-comment reference omits the ‘Re:’ title lead-in, the ‘[blog comment]’ designation or the blog name.
when: The cited source is a comment on a blog post.
rules.why: The comment template adds a distinct source-identification format.

covers.quote: Use the poster’s name and the first 10 words of the content followed by an ellipsis in the short citation where the title would normally be.

rules.quote: For social media posts, include the first 10 words of the content followed by an ellipsis if there’s no title.
rules.violation_condition: An untitled social-media reference does not substitute the first 10 content words followed by an ellipsis, or its short citation does not use that content excerpt in the title position.
when: For a full citation, use the excerpt when the post has no title.
For a short citation, the page specifies the poster's name and first 10 content words followed by an ellipsis.
rules.why: G-2: full and short citations determine when the same content-excerpt title form applies.

rules.quote: Make sure you let the user know you’re citing a social media post before you insert a reference marker.
rules.violation_condition: The text introduces a social-media reference marker without first identifying the source as a social media post.
when: The cited source is a social media post.
rules.why: This requires identifiable information in the text, not merely a writer action.

rules.quote: Rule: Name of Page or Poster, ‘Title or first 10 words of content of post ...' [type of post], Page of Post, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.
rules.violation_condition: A social-media or forum-post reference omits the page or poster, bracketed post type or page of the post.
when: The cited source is a social-media or online-forum post.
rules.why: Keep the post's source-identification structure distinct from excerpt length, dates and hyperlinking.

covers.quote: For dictionaries and encyclopaedias, mention them in the text but don’t include a note.

rules.quote: For emails and personal communication, mention them in the text but don’t include a note.
rules.violation_condition: An email, personal communication, dictionary or encyclopaedia is cited in a documentary note instead of being identified in the text.
when: The cited source is an email, personal communication, dictionary or encyclopaedia.
rules.why: G-2: the listed source types share the same inline-only citation treatment.

covers.quote: Rule: I Interviewer, Interviewer Full Name interviews Interviewee Full Name: Title of interview [interview audio or video file], Name of Publisher, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.
The interviewer’s name always comes first in the reference.
Use the name of the interviewer in short citations.

rules.quote: Rule: I Interviewer, Interviewer Full Name interviews Interviewee Full Name: Title of interview [interview transcript], Name of Publisher, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.
rules.violation_condition: An interview citation fails to lead with the interviewer, omits the interviewer–interviewee identification or format designation, or uses the interviewee rather than interviewer in a short citation.
when: For transcripts, use ‘[interview transcript]’.
For audio or video, use the corresponding interview-file designation.
Short citations use the interviewer's name.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: interview medium and citation length are cases of the same interview attribution structure.

rules.quote: If you're quoting the interviewee, make it clear in the text.
rules.violation_condition: An interviewee's quotation is presented without making clear in the surrounding text that the interviewee, rather than interviewer, is speaking.
when: The text quotes the interviewee.
rules.why: In-text speaker attribution is distinct from the note's interviewer-first structure.

rules.quote: Rule: A Author, ‘Title of article: subtitle of article’, Name of Journal, in press.
rules.violation_condition: A citation to a journal article accepted but not yet published omits ‘in press’ or presents it as an already published article.
when: The journal article has been accepted for publication but is not yet published.
rules.why: Publication status introduces a distinct prescribed replacement for publication details.

covers.quote: Rule: A Author, ‘Title of paper: subtitle of paper’ [unpublished conference presentation], Name of Conference, Place of Conference, Day Month Year.

rules.quote: Rule: A Author, ‘Title of paper: subtitle of paper’ [conference presentation], Name of Conference, Place of Conference, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.
rules.violation_condition: A conference-paper reference omits the presentation designation, conference name or conference location, or fails to distinguish an unpublished presentation.
when: Use ‘[conference presentation]’ for the published form.
Use ‘[unpublished conference presentation]’ for an unpublished paper.
Include an access date when accessed online.
rules.why: G-2: publication status changes the same conference-reference form.

covers.quote: Rule: A Author, Title of thesis: subtitle of thesis [unpublished type of thesis], Name of University, Year, accessed Day Month Year.

rules.quote: Rule: A Author, Title of thesis: subtitle of thesis [type of thesis] Name of University, Year, accessed Day Month Year.
rules.violation_condition: A thesis reference omits its bracketed thesis type or university, or fails to identify the thesis as unpublished when applicable.
when: Use the thesis type in brackets.
For an unpublished thesis, include ‘unpublished’ in that designation.
Access dates apply to sources accessed online.
rules.why: G-2: published and unpublished theses are cases of one thesis-identification check.

rules.quote: Rule: A Author, Title of book, subtitle of book, Xth edn, Name of Publisher, Place of Publication, Year.
rules.specification: The page shows the edition format but does not expressly state whether a first edition must be identified.
rules.violation_condition: A reference requiring identification of a book edition omits the edition or fails to present it as an ordinal followed by ‘edn’ between title and publisher.
when: An edition is identified in a book reference.
rules.why: The edition element adds a specific requirement beyond common book-reference structure.

rules.quote: Rule: E Editor (ed), Title of book: subtitle of book,Name of Publisher, Place of Publication, Year.

covers.quote: If you’re citing a PDF, avoid linking directly to the PDF. Instead link to the page that hosts the PDF.

tags.violation_condition: A citation links directly to a PDF or other downloadable document when a hosting landing page is available.

when: A hosting or landing page exists.
If a PDF has no landing page, link directly to the PDF.
The page repeats the hosting-page preference for spreadsheets and other downloadable documents.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: consolidate the repeated link-target preference and no-landing-page exception.

anchor.quote: If the PDF doesn’t have a landing page, link to the PDF and include ‘PDF’ in square brackets after the title.
anchor.suffix: Follow ‘PDF’ with the file size

covers.quote: Follow ‘PDF’ with the file size in kilobytes (KB) or megabytes (MB).
Include both of these additional details in the linked text.

tags.violation_condition: A direct PDF citation without a landing page lacks the bracketed PDF label and KB or MB file size after the title, or leaves those details outside the linked text.

when: The PDF has no landing page and is linked directly.
rules.why: G-2: label, size and link extent define one direct-PDF link presentation.

anchor.quote: If the document has a DOI, include it in the citation. Put it at the end of the citation and include the shortened form ‘doi’ in lower case before it.

covers.quote: For journal articles, include the DOI if possible.
Include a DOI if the book has one.
covers.suffix: Only include the place of publi

tags.violation_condition: A source with a DOI lacks it in the citation, places it somewhere other than the end, or uses a prefix other than lower-case ‘doi’.

when: The cited document has a DOI.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: consolidate DOI inclusion and presentation across source types.

anchor.quote: To cite a specific page or page range in a work, add:

covers.quote: the letter ‘p’ and the page number to cite one page
the letters ‘pp’ and the page number range to cite a range of pages.

tags.violation_condition: A specific-page locator lacks ‘p’ before one page number or ‘pp’ before a page range, or uses the wrong one.

when: The locator identifies a specific page or page range, rather than the journal article's publication page span.
rules.why: G-2: single-page and page-range cases determine one locator-prefix check.

anchor.quote: If the citation has a volume number, an issue number and page numbers follow the format: volume(issue):page–page.

tags.violation_condition: A citation containing volume, issue and page numbers does not present them as volume(issue):page–page.

when: The citation contains a volume number, issue number and page numbers.
rules.why: This is a specific internal numerical-format check.

anchor.quote: To cite a specific page of this work, add the page number at the end.

tags.violation_condition: A citation to a specific page of an article with a publication page range omits the additional pinpoint page or places it before the end.

when: A particular page within the cited article is being referenced.
rules.why: Pinpoint placement is distinct from formatting the article's publication page range.

anchor.quote: Rule: A Author and B Author, Title of media release: subtitle of media release [media release], Organisation Name, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.

covers.quote: Rule: Organisation Name Title of media release: subtitle of media release [media release], Organisation Name, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.

tags.violation_condition: A media-release reference omits its ‘[media release]’ designation or issuing organisation, or assigns the author role incorrectly when no personal author is listed.

when: Use listed personal authors when present.
With no listed authors, use the organisation as author.
Apply the general date, access-date, hyperlink and punctuation rules separately.
rules.why: G-2: author availability changes the same media-release citation structure.

anchor.quote: Follow the authoring details on the title page of the document.

tags.violation_condition: A report citation's authoring details disagree with the report's title page.

when: The source has a title page.
rules.why: The instruction defines the authoritative source for a text property.

anchor.quote: Rule: A Author or Agency Name (Abbreviation), Title of report: subtitle of report, Agency Name or Abbreviation, Name of Government, Year, accessed Day Month Year.

covers.quote: Rule: A Author or Agency Name (Abbreviation), Title of report: subtitle of report, Agency Name or Abbreviation, Name of Government, unpublished, accessed Day Month Year.

tags.violation_condition: A reference to a government-agency report omits the agency or name of government, or fails to identify an unpublished agency report as ‘unpublished’ in the date position.

when: The report is by a government agency.
Use the unpublished variant when the report is unpublished.
Access dates apply to sources accessed online.
rules.why: G-2: publication status changes the same government-report format.

anchor.quote: Rule: A Author or Agency Name (Abbreviation), ‘Title of report: subtitle of report’, Name of Series, catalogue number, Agency Name or Abbreviation, Name of Government, Year, accessed Day Month Year.

tags.violation_condition: A report-in-series reference omits the series name or catalogue number, or places those series details outside their position between report title and agency.

when: The government report is part of a series.
rules.why: Keep the additional series-identification check distinct from general government-report details.

anchor.quote: Rule: A Author or Organisation Name (Abbreviation), Title of report: subtitle of report, report to Agency Name, Organisation Name or Abbreviation, Year.

tags.violation_condition: A report prepared for a government agency fails to identify the recipient with ‘report to’ after the title or omits the producing organisation.

when: The report was prepared for a government agency by an external author or organisation.
rules.why: The recipient relationship is an additional source-specific element.

anchor.quote: Rule: Name of Parliament, Title of document: subtitle of document, Parl Paper X, Name of Government, Year.

covers.quote: use the name of the parliament as the author
include the paper number.

tags.violation_condition: A document cited from a bound parliamentary volume does not use the parliament as author or omits its ‘Parl Paper’ number or government identification.

when: The document was accessed as part of a bound volume from a parliamentary sitting.
Individually accessed documents use their ordinary document-type citation instead.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: consolidate the bound-volume instructions and their template.

anchor.quote: Rule: Name of Parliamentary Committee or House, Debates, Year, volume:page–page.

covers.quote: To cite a record of what was said in parliament verbatim, as recorded in Hansard, use the volume and page number. Volume numbers are before the colon; page numbers are after.

tags.violation_condition: A Hansard reference omits the committee or house, ‘Debates’, volume or page locator, or fails to put volume before and pages after a colon.

when: The source is a verbatim parliamentary record in Hansard.
rules.why: G-4: the prose and template specify one Hansard locator structure.

anchor.quote: Rule: Name of Parliamentary House, Journalor Votes and Proceedings, Year, (issue) or volume:page–page.

covers.quote: To cite the official records of proceedings in each house of parliament, include the volume or issue number and the page number. Issue numbers are in parentheses. Volume numbers are outside of parentheses.

tags.violation_condition: An official parliamentary-proceedings reference omits its house, record title, volume or issue, or pages, or puts a volume in parentheses or leaves an issue outside parentheses.

when: The source is an official record of proceedings in a parliamentary house.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: issue and volume are alternative cases of the same proceedings locator.

anchor.quote: Rule: A Author, Title of data set [data set], Name of Website website, Year, accessed Day Month Year.

tags.violation_condition: A data-set reference lacks the ‘[data set]’ designation after its title.

when: The source is a data set; apply source-specific ABS instructions where relevant.
rules.why: The designation is the additional requirement not already covered by common reference structure.

anchor.quote: Follow the ABS advice for information to include, but adjust capitalisation and punctuation to be in line with the rest of the notes in your content.

tags.specification: The required source-specific information must be obtained from the ABS guide; this page supplies only the adaptation principle.
tags.violation_condition: A reference to ABS material omits information required by ABS referencing advice or retains ABS capitalisation and punctuation that conflict with the surrounding documentary–note style.

when: The cited material is from the Australian Bureau of Statistics.
rules.why: G-2: ABS information requirements apply with an explicit local-style adjustment.

anchor.quote: Follow this advice exactly, but add a full stop at the end of the citation.

tags.specification: The external NAA guide supplies the exact format. Final full-stop absence is handled by the general final-punctuation rule.
tags.violation_condition: A reference to an NAA-held record departs from the National Archives of Australia's prescribed referencing format.

when: The source is a record held by the National Archives of Australia.
rules.why: G-2: preserve the externally specified citation format and the stated punctuation adjustment.

anchor.quote: Only cite an entire website if you cannot pinpoint the material to a specific webpage or webpage content.

covers.quote: However, if you refer to content only found on a particular webpage on the website, you need to pinpoint the relevant webpage or webpage content in the citation.

tags.violation_condition: A citation identifies only an entire website although the referenced material can be pinpointed to a particular webpage or content item.

when: An entire-website citation is acceptable for a general resource that cannot be pinpointed.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: both sentences govern the same citation-specificity decision.

anchor.quote: Use the same capitalisation as the organisation uses for the name of a website.

covers.quote: Use the same capitalisation as the organisation uses for the name of a website.

tags.violation_condition: A cited website name uses different capitalisation from the organisation's own form.

when: A website name appears in a reference.
rules.why: G-4: consolidate the identical website-name capitalisation instructions.

anchor.quote: Include the word ‘website’ after the name of the website in square brackets, unless you include the URL for the homepage.

covers.quote: If you include the homepage URL, do not include the word ‘website’ in square brackets.
Include the word ‘website’ after the name of the website, unless the name of the website is a URL – for example ‘WA.gov.au’.
When citing a document hosted on a webpage, but not the webpage itself, don’t include the word ‘website’ in the citation.

tags.violation_condition: An online reference omits or misformats the required website designation, retains ‘[website]’ beside an entire-site homepage URL, or adds ‘website’ when citing an online document rather than the webpage.

when: An entire-site reference uses ‘[website]’ after the website name unless a homepage URL is included.
A webpage reference uses ‘website’ without square brackets after the website name, unless that name is itself a URL.
A reference to a document hosted on a webpage does not include ‘website’.
rules.why: G-2: cited-object type and URL presentation determine one website-designation check.

anchor.quote: For videos published online, hyperlink the title of the video and file format.

tags.violation_condition: An online-video reference's hyperlink excludes the file-format designation.

when: The reference is to a video published online.
rules.why: The link's extension over the format label is additional to the general title-link requirement.

anchor.quote: Rule: C Creator or Owner of Video, ‘Title of video’ [video], Name of Channel or Owning Organisation, Name of Website website, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.

tags.violation_condition: An online-video citation omits its creator or owner, ‘[video]’ designation, or channel or owning organisation, or puts those identifying elements in the wrong roles.

when: The cited source is an online video.
rules.why: Retain the source-specific creator, medium and channel structure without duplicating common date and link checks.

anchor.quote: For tables and images (such as graphs) you’re using in the content, attribute the source in the notes below the table or image (also called a ‘figure’).

tags.violation_condition: A reproduced table or image has no source attribution in notes below it, or places that attribution in its caption or title instead.

rules.why: G-2 and G-4: required and prohibited attribution locations form one placement check.

anchor.quote: Don’t include this information or a reference marker in the caption or title to the table or figure.

tags.violation_condition: A table or figure caption or title contains a reference marker.

when: The table or figure is reproduced in the content.
rules.why: A prohibited marker can occur independently of correctly placed source-attribution notes.

anchor.quote: Rule: Source: Adapted from Source.

tags.specification: Apply ‘Adapted from’ to adapted material, not indiscriminately to unchanged reproductions.
tags.violation_condition: A source note for an adapted table or figure does not identify the source with ‘Source: Adapted from’.

when: The table or figure has been adapted from another source.
rules.why: The template prescribes the source-note lead-in; its adaptation wording limits applicability.

anchor.quote: Rule: Creator Full Name, Title or description of work [medium], Name of Website website, Exhibition or Gallery, Location of Gallery, Year, © Creator, courtesy: Creator or Gallery, accessed Date Month Year.

covers.quote: Attribute works of art (such as photographs) using an extended caption that includes:
the full details of the work of art
copyright and permission information if necessary.

tags.violation_condition: A reproduced work of art lacks an extended caption giving its creator's full name, title or description, medium and applicable identifying, copyright or permission details.

when: The work of art, such as a photograph or illustration, is used in the content.
Include gallery, location, website, copyright and permission details as applicable.
If merely discussing the work without reproducing it, use an ordinary reference marker and note.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: consolidate the artwork-caption instruction, its required details and template.

anchor.quote: Rule: A Author, ‘Title of article: subtitle of article’, Name of Blog, Newspaper or Magazine, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.

covers.quote: If a post or article doesn’t list an author, use the name of the blog, newspaper or magazine.
Rule: Name of Blog, Newspaper or Magazine, ‘Title of article: subtitle of article’, Name of Newspaper or Magazine, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.

tags.violation_condition: A blog-post, newspaper or magazine reference omits its publication name or fails to use the publication as author when no author is listed.

when: Use a listed author where one exists.
If no author is listed, use the blog, newspaper or magazine name as author.
rules.why: G-2: listed-author and no-author cases belong to one publication-attribution check.

anchor.quote: Rule: A Author, ‘Re: Title of post: subtitle of post’ [blog comment], Name of Blog, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.

tags.violation_condition: A blog-comment reference omits the ‘Re:’ title lead-in, the ‘[blog comment]’ designation or the blog name.

when: The cited source is a comment on a blog post.
rules.why: The comment template adds a distinct source-identification format.

anchor.quote: For social media posts, include the first 10 words of the content followed by an ellipsis if there’s no title.
anchor.suffix: Hyperlink the content or title

covers.quote: Use the poster’s name and the first 10 words of the content followed by an ellipsis in the short citation where the title would normally be.

tags.violation_condition: An untitled social-media reference does not substitute the first 10 content words followed by an ellipsis, or its short citation does not use that content excerpt in the title position.

when: For a full citation, use the excerpt when the post has no title.
For a short citation, the page specifies the poster's name and first 10 content words followed by an ellipsis.
rules.why: G-2: full and short citations determine when the same content-excerpt title form applies.

anchor.quote: Make sure you let the user know you’re citing a social media post before you insert a reference marker.

tags.violation_condition: The text introduces a social-media reference marker without first identifying the source as a social media post.

when: The cited source is a social media post.
rules.why: This requires identifiable information in the text, not merely a writer action.

anchor.quote: Rule: Name of Page or Poster, ‘Title or first 10 words of content of post ...' [type of post], Page of Post, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.

tags.violation_condition: A social-media or forum-post reference omits the page or poster, bracketed post type or page of the post.

when: The cited source is a social-media or online-forum post.
rules.why: Keep the post's source-identification structure distinct from excerpt length, dates and hyperlinking.

anchor.quote: For emails and personal communication, mention them in the text but don’t include a note.

covers.quote: For dictionaries and encyclopaedias, mention them in the text but don’t include a note.

tags.violation_condition: An email, personal communication, dictionary or encyclopaedia is cited in a documentary note instead of being identified in the text.

when: The cited source is an email, personal communication, dictionary or encyclopaedia.
rules.why: G-2: the listed source types share the same inline-only citation treatment.

anchor.quote: Rule: I Interviewer, Interviewer Full Name interviews Interviewee Full Name: Title of interview [interview transcript], Name of Publisher, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.

covers.quote: Rule: I Interviewer, Interviewer Full Name interviews Interviewee Full Name: Title of interview [interview audio or video file], Name of Publisher, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.
The interviewer’s name always comes first in the reference.
Use the name of the interviewer in short citations.

tags.violation_condition: An interview citation fails to lead with the interviewer, omits the interviewer–interviewee identification or format designation, or uses the interviewee rather than interviewer in a short citation.

when: For transcripts, use ‘[interview transcript]’.
For audio or video, use the corresponding interview-file designation.
Short citations use the interviewer's name.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4: interview medium and citation length are cases of the same interview attribution structure.

anchor.prefix: s comes first in the reference.
anchor.quote: If you're quoting the interviewee, make it clear in the text.

tags.violation_condition: An interviewee's quotation is presented without making clear in the surrounding text that the interviewee, rather than interviewer, is speaking.

when: The text quotes the interviewee.
rules.why: In-text speaker attribution is distinct from the note's interviewer-first structure.

anchor.quote: Rule: A Author, ‘Title of article: subtitle of article’, Name of Journal, in press.

tags.violation_condition: A citation to a journal article accepted but not yet published omits ‘in press’ or presents it as an already published article.

when: The journal article has been accepted for publication but is not yet published.
rules.why: Publication status introduces a distinct prescribed replacement for publication details.

anchor.quote: Rule: A Author, ‘Title of paper: subtitle of paper’ [conference presentation], Name of Conference, Place of Conference, Day Month Year, accessed Day Month Year.

covers.quote: Rule: A Author, ‘Title of paper: subtitle of paper’ [unpublished conference presentation], Name of Conference, Place of Conference, Day Month Year.

tags.violation_condition: A conference-paper reference omits the presentation designation, conference name or conference location, or fails to distinguish an unpublished presentation.

when: Use ‘[conference presentation]’ for the published form.
Use ‘[unpublished conference presentation]’ for an unpublished paper.
Include an access date when accessed online.
rules.why: G-2: publication status changes the same conference-reference form.

anchor.quote: Rule: A Author, Title of thesis: subtitle of thesis [type of thesis] Name of University, Year, accessed Day Month Year.

covers.quote: Rule: A Author, Title of thesis: subtitle of thesis [unpublished type of thesis], Name of University, Year, accessed Day Month Year.

tags.violation_condition: A thesis reference omits its bracketed thesis type or university, or fails to identify the thesis as unpublished when applicable.

when: Use the thesis type in brackets.
For an unpublished thesis, include ‘unpublished’ in that designation.
Access dates apply to sources accessed online.
rules.why: G-2: published and unpublished theses are cases of one thesis-identification check.

anchor.quote: Rule: A Author, Title of book, subtitle of book, Xth edn, Name of Publisher, Place of Publication, Year.

tags.specification: The page shows the edition format but does not expressly state whether a first edition must be identified.
tags.violation_condition: A reference requiring identification of a book edition omits the edition or fails to present it as an ordinal followed by ‘edn’ between title and publisher.

when: An edition is identified in a book reference.
rules.why: The edition element adds a specific requirement beyond common book-reference structure.

anchor.quote: Rule: E Editor (ed), Title of book: subtitle of book,Name of Publisher, Place of Publication, Year.

tags.violation_condition: A book compiled by editors fails to identify them in the leading creator position with ‘(ed)’ for one editor or ‘(eds)’ for multiple editors.

when: The book is compiled by editors rather than attributed to authors.
rules.why: Editor-role notation is the distinct requirement of this template.

anchor.quote: Rule: A Author, ‘Title of chapter: subtitle of chapter’, in E Editor and F Editor (eds) Title of book: subtitle of book, Name of Publisher, Place of Publication, Year.

tags.violation_condition: A chapter-in-edited-book reference omits the ‘in’ relationship, the book's editors or their editor-role designation, or fails to identify the containing book.

when: The cited source is a chapter in an edited book.
rules.why: The chapter-to-container relationship is additional to general title and author formatting.

anchor.quote: Rule: A Author, Title of book: subtitle of book(E Editor ed), Name of Publisher, Place of Publication, Year.

tags.violation_condition: A book reference with an author and editor omits the editor or fails to place the parenthetical editor name and ‘ed’ after the title.

when: The book lists both an author and an editor.
rules.why: This template specifies a different editor role and location from an editor-compiled book.

anchor.quote: Rule: A Author, English title of book (T Translator trans), Name of Publisher, Place of Publication, Year.

covers.quote: In the short citation for translated works, use the original author’s name and the English title of the work.

tags.violation_condition: A translated-book reference omits its English title or parenthetical translator credit with ‘trans’, or a short citation replaces the original author with the translator.

when: The cited book is a translation.
Short citations use the original author's name and English title.
rules.why: G-2: full and short forms preserve the same original-author and translated-title roles.

anchor.quote: Only include the place of publication if it’s relevant to the user.

covers.prefix: lude a DOI if the book has one.
covers.quote: Only include the place of publication if it’s relevant to the user
you’re citing works with editions published in multiple locations
the location the book was published impacts the credibility of your work.
If the place of publication doesn’t add useful information for the user, you can omit it from your citation.
If you include a DOI, you don’t need to include a publishing location.

tags.specification: Relevance is contextual; the page gives examples rather than an exhaustive test.
tags.violation_condition: A book citation includes a publication location that adds no useful information for the user.

when: Location may be relevant for editions published in multiple places or where it affects credibility.
An irrelevant location can be omitted.
A book citation with a DOI does not need a publication location.
rules.why: G-2, G-3 and G-4: consolidate the relevance restriction, examples of relevance and omission permissions.

anchor.quote: For unpublished works such as internal documents, include the year the work was written where you would usually have the year the work was published.

tags.violation_condition: An unpublished-work reference omits its writing year or puts something else in the usual publication-year position.

when: The work is unpublished, such as an internal document.
Apply the separately specified unpublished-government-report format where relevant.
rules.why: G-2: unpublished status changes the meaning of the citation's year field.

anchor.quote: Rule: A Author Title of document: subtitle of document [unpublished type of document], Organisation Name, Writing Location, Year.

tags.violation_condition: An unpublished-document reference omits its bracketed unpublished document type, organisation or writing location.

when: The source is an unpublished work covered by this general template.
rules.why: The template adds document-status and writing-location details beyond the separate year rule.

anchor.quote: Rule: A Author, Title of publication: subtitle of publication [printed type of publication], Name of Publisher or Owning Organisation, Place of Publication, Year.

tags.violation_condition: A reference to another printed publication omits its bracketed printed-publication type, publisher or owning organisation, or publication place.

when: The source is another printed publication, such as a printed brochure, rather than a source with a more specific template.
rules.why: Retain the printed-publication designation and source-specific location requirement.
